fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Garage; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Retaining Wall; Access Drive; Open Lawn Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access; Fenced Sections
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responding units can identify it quickly under low-light or smoky conditions.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance for fire apparatus and emergency vehicles on both sides.
• Cut back dense vegetation that grows close to the main residence to reduce the risk of fire spreading directly to the structure.
• Thin dense vegetation areas to create gaps that prevent fire from moving continuously from the yard to the buildings.
• Keep a clear path along the exterior walls of the main residence so responders can move around the building on foot.
• Identify a secondary exit point from the property and keep it passable for foot traffic in the event the driveway is blocked.
• Post a property map or diagram near the driveway entrance showing the location of the detached garage, access drive, and any locked gates.
• Keep any gates in fenced sections unlocked or secured with a break-away lock so responders can reach the rear of the property without delay.
• Clear a staging area near the driveway large enough for a fire engine to park and turn around without backing onto the road.
• Mark the location of any exterior utility shutoffs on the detached garage or main residence so responders can find them quickly.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Brush Area; Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Mixed Vegetation; Single Access Route; Limited Rear Access; Scattered Trees; Grass Cover; Open Terrain; Woody Debris
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove brush and shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure on all sides.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees and the building.
• Clear woody debris, including fallen branches and dead wood, from the ground around the structure.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near the structure so branches do not hang close to the ground or roofline.
• Mow or cut grass cover in the open terrain surrounding the structure, particularly on the approach side.
• Remove or thin mixed vegetation that connects ground-level plants to shrubs to taller trees near the structure.
• Clear shrubs and overhanging branches along the single access driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway surface and edges free of woody debris and dead plant material that could block emergency vehicle movement.
• Cut back vegetation along the rear of the property to open a path for movement around the back of the structure.
• Separate shrub groupings in the scatter areas around the structure so open gaps exist between plant clusters and the building.
• Remove dead material from within shrubs near the structure, including dry stems and dead interior branches.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding any outbuildings or detached structures clear of brush, grass, and woody debris.
